To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the structure of the DNA binding domain of the small subunit of the bacteriophages bacteriophage SF-6 terminase is presented; (2) the DNA binding domain consists of a helix-hairpin-helix motif; (3) the structure of this DNA binding domain has been determined by x-ray crystallography at 1.58 A resolution and (4) this structure is compared to other DNA-binding proteins.
the structure of the N terminal domain of the small terminase of the Bacillus phage SF6 has been solved and the structure has been compared with other DNA binding proteins.
the DNA binding domain of the bacterio-phage SF6 small terminas subunit G1p has a novel fold and binds the packaging initiation site in a novel way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural analysis of proteins involved in DNA packaging in tetraviruses, bacteriophages, and herpesviruses.
the structure and function of the small subunit of terminase, which is the DNA-binding protein that recognizes the origin of packaging in tailed viruses.
the structural analysis of the DNA packaging machinery in bacteriophages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G1P is a novel member of the HNH nuclease family and that it has an additional DNA-binding function.

G1P binds DNA through the N-terminal domain and that the DNA-binding site is formed by two helices, H1 and H3, and a β-sheet, β2, and that the DNA is bound by the positively charged side chains of R3, R5, R7, K10, R11, R13 and R15.
the G1P-DNA complex structure provides new insights into the DNA binding mechanism of the SF6 small terminaser and, in general, of the terminase family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
G1P binds DNA by a combination of electrostatic interactions, hydrophobic contacts and hydrogen bonds.

the SF6 small terminaseresidues 1–90 are a DNA binding domain, and that the SF6 terminase DNA-binding site is located at the 5′-end of the phage DNA, and that the terminase binds to the DNA at the 5'-end of the DNA.
we have solved the structure of a DNA-binding domain of a small terminase sub-unit, that is a key component in the DNA-packing machinery of many tailed bacteriophage.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structure of the DNA binding domain of the small subunit of the bacteriophages SPP1 and SF6 terminase complex is similar to the structure of the NTP-binding domain of the large subunit of the same complex.
the DNA-binding domain in the SF6 terminase subunit has a structure that is very similar to the DNA-binding domains of the other phage terminase subunits.
the DNA-binding domain in the small subunit of the bacteriophages SPP1 and SF6 terminase is structurally similar to the DNA-binding domain found in the small subunits of other phages.
